notes: Egypt is the simplest converted arena: six doors, six spawns and almost no destructible clutter. It is wide open stone rooms, which makes it the converted map that plays most like Temple and least like Facility.
See mp/_general.json for the cross-arena layer.

nuance.claim: The stage is large open chambers with very little furniture, so there is almost nothing to hide behind and fights are decided at range in the open.
nuance.because: The arena carries no StandardProp or Glass records at all, unlike every other converted stage.

nuance.claim: With only six doors, the connections between areas are few and obvious, so movement is highly predictable and worth watching.
nuance.because: The arena carries six Door records, fewest of any converted stage and a sixth of Bunker's thirty-six.

nuance.claim: Because there are so few connections, a handful of mines covers essentially all movement between areas, which is a far higher return than on the door-dense maps.
nuance.because: Six Door records is the smallest connection set of any converted arena.

nuance.claim: Six spawn points in a moderate space makes spawn pressure viable, particularly with the few doors funnelling movement afterwards.
nuance.because: The arena carries six Spawn records against eight on Facility and Archives.

nuance.claim: Long clear lines across open stone rooms make precision weapons unusually effective, and there is little cover to break the shot.
The rooms are large enough to fire explosives at range without self-damage, making those sets viable in a way they are not on the tight conversions.
With few doors and no clutter, disengaging is hard: a fight that starts usually finishes, so committing to one should be a decision rather than an accident.
Pickups are the normalised conversion set, so armour is convenient rather than contested and position is the only real advantage.
nuance.because: The arena carries the standard conversion loadout of two Armour, sixteen AmmoBox and nine Collectable records.

nuance.claim: Against pale stone at the ranges this map fights at, a dark character is the more visible one, so lighter choices are better here.
One-hit kills with no cover and long lines make crossing a room close to suicide, so the mode collapses into holding doorways and waiting.
An unarmed carrier has no cover to break line of sight with and few routes to take, so holds here are the shortest of any arena.
A one-shot weapon in a map with long open sightlines and no cover is overwhelming, so contesting the initial pickup matters more here than anywhere else.
